title: Think Big Undergraduate Scholarships
program_type: University merit scholarship awarded at admission, applied as a tuition-fee discount through a separate scholarship application
implementing_agency: University of Bristol international scholarships team (international-scholarships@bristol.ac.uk)
programme_action: Think Big scholarship scheme - standard and subject-specific undergraduate tuition-fee discount awards (Think Big about Business, Economics, Policy Studies, Science and Engineering, Veterinary Science)
description: Think Big is the University of Bristol's flagship scholarship scheme and provides funding towards tuition fees for international students on eligible undergraduate courses. Undergraduate awards are worth £6,500 or £13,000 for each year of study, applied as a tuition fee discount for up to four years, and are funded entirely by the University (up to £5 million invested in the scheme for 2026 entry). Applicants submit one online scholarship application, which is matched to their UCAS study application and assessed for every Think Big award for which they are eligible, including subject-specific awards. Successful recipients also join the Think Big Development Programme, a networking and leadership programme.

programme_structure.award_types_detail: Standard undergraduate awards are valued at £6,500 and £13,000 per year. Subject-specific undergraduate awards published for 2026 entry: Think Big about Business £6,500 (Business School); Think Big about Economics £6,500 (School of Economics); Think Big about Policy Studies £13,000 (School for Policy Studies); Think Big about Science and Engineering £6,500 (Chemistry BSc and Physics BSc within the Faculty of Science and Engineering); Think Big about Veterinary Science £6,500 (BVSc and BVSc Accelerated Graduate Entry, funding available for only three years of full-time study). Subject-specific awards are reviewed annually and can change.
programme_structure.renewal_criteria: The tuition fee discount is applied each year the student pays full fees, up to a maximum of four years, and is renewed each year provided the student makes satisfactory progress, defined by the University as an average mark above 50% each year. The discount is not applied in years not spent at the University (for example a placement year in industry or a year of study abroad) or during suspension of studies. Funding for repeat or supplementary study is reviewed case by case.
programme_structure.automatic_consideration: Partly automatic within the scheme: one scholarship application form is submitted, and the applicant is considered for every Think Big award for which they meet the eligibility requirements. It is not automatic on admission - a separate scholarship application is required.
programme_structure.intake: September entry only (2026-entry awards valid for September 2026 only and cannot be deferred)

programme_duration.official_range: Scholarship funding is applied for each year of study up to a maximum of four years for standard undergraduate awards; the undergraduate degrees themselves run 3 to 4 years full-time (longer for integrated master's such as MSci/MArts and for BVSc Veterinary Science, for which the Think Big about Veterinary Science award funds only three years).
programme_duration.renewal_note: Renewed each year for up to four years provided the student makes satisfactory progress, defined as an average mark above 50% each year, and continues to pay full fees. No funding is applied during placement, study-abroad or suspension years.

funding.monthly_amount_note: No monthly stipend or maintenance payment is published. The award is applied as a reduction to tuition fees at enrolment and there is no cash alternative.
funding.travel_amount_note: No travel or installation payment is published. Applicants must fund their own travel, visa and Immigration Health Surcharge costs.
funding.fully_funded_note: Not fully funded. Awards cover tuition fees only, at £6,500 or £13,000 per year for up to four years. International tuition fees are set per course and reviewed annually (increases capped at 8% per year, not applied to clinical courses). The University reports average undergraduate living costs of £1,401 per month in 2025/26, which this award does not cover.
funding.scheme_total_investment: Up to £5 million invested in Think Big scholarships for 2026 entry (up to £6 million was stated for 2025 entry). The number of individual undergraduate awards is not published.

tuition.duration: up to four years (standard undergraduate awards); three years for Think Big about Veterinary Science
tuition.conditions: Applied as a discount to tuition fees at enrolment; no cash alternative; any amount in excess of the tuition fee due is not paid out. Renewed each year provided satisfactory progress (average mark above 50%). Cannot be combined with other University-funded tuition fee discounts; only the award or discount of higher value is applied (Alumni Discount excepted).

accommodation_support.note: No accommodation support is provided by the award. Bursaries that do carry living-cost support (for example the Michael Wong Pakshong bursary) are postgraduate awards and are not part of the undergraduate Think Big offer.

bond.note: No service bond or repayment obligation is published. Recipients are expected to be ambassadors of the University, to engage with the Think Big Development Programme, and may be invited to promotional activity limited to a maximum of 10 hours per semester.

total_estimated_value.note: The University publishes per-year award values (£6,500 or £13,000) but no total award value. A total is not computed here because it depends on award value, number of years funded and tuition fees.

coverage: Tuition fee discount of £6,500 or £13,000 per year
Discount applied for each year of study, up to a maximum of four years (three years for Think Big about Veterinary Science)
Access to the Think Big Development Programme (welcome reception and workshop series) for all Think Big recipients
Opportunity to apply for paid Think Big student ambassador roles
One scholarship application assessed for every Think Big award, including subject-specific awards, for which the applicant is eligible
coverage_limitations: Tuition-fee discount only. No living allowance, travel, installation, visa, insurance or family support is provided.
No cash alternative: the discount is applied to tuition fees at enrolment, and any amount exceeding tuition fees is not paid to the student.
The discount is not applied in years not spent at the University (for example placement or study-abroad years) or during suspension of studies.
Cannot be combined with other University-funded tuition fee discounts; only the award or discount of higher value is applied (Alumni Discount is the single exception).

Living stipends and bursaries may be received alongside the award, but total external funding including Think Big must not exceed tuition fees; external full-tuition funding makes the applicant ineligible.
Awards are valid for September entry of the named year only and cannot be deferred to a later year.
Subject-specific awards are reviewed each year and can change, so the exact benefit structure for the 2027 entry cycle may differ from the values published for 2026 entry.
Courses in Bristol Dental School and Bristol Medical School are not eligible.
eligible_applicants: Applicants for a full-time, in-person undergraduate course at the University of Bristol who are classed as overseas students for fee-paying purposes
Applicants of any nationality (no country quota applies to the standard Think Big undergraduate awards)
Applicants who have already applied to study at Bristol through UCAS and hold an application ID (UCAS ID); an offer is not needed at the point of scholarship application
Final-year secondary school applicants, including applicants with gap years and mature students, provided the course and fee-status conditions are met
final_year_condition: Applicants normally apply while in their final year of secondary school or holding a recent school-leaving qualification. For the 2026-entry round the applicant had to have received an offer from Bristol before Friday 24 April 2026 (otherwise the scholarship application was withdrawn), meet or exceed the entry requirements stated in their formal UCAS offer before 31 August 2026, and confirm the University of Bristol as their Firm choice in UCAS.
equivalent_degree_note: Bristol accepts a wide range of international school-leaving and non-UK qualifications for undergraduate entry, with typical offers published per course in the online course finder. Applications are considered on individual merit and entry requirements shown are indicative; a formal offer may differ slightly from the published typical offer.

age_limit.official_source: No age limit is published for Think Big undergraduate scholarships. The University separately welcomes mature students aged 21 or over when starting an undergraduate degree.

eligibility.citizenship: No nationality restriction for the standard Think Big undergraduate awards. Subject-specific awards are restricted by subject area rather than nationality.
eligibility.residence_requirement: Applicants must be classified as overseas students for fee-paying purposes. Fee status is determined by immigration status and residence history under UK Government regulations, with guidance from UKCISA; it cannot be assessed before an application is submitted.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Applicants must have applied for, or hold, a place on a full-time in-person undergraduate course. Entry requirements are set per course and stated in the applicant's formal UCAS offer; applicants normally apply during their final year of secondary school.
eligibility.academic_requirements: The scholarship itself sets no separate grade threshold. Applicants must meet or exceed the entry requirements stated in their formal UCAS offer before 31 August of the entry year (2026-entry rule).
eligibility.gpa_requirement: No GPA, percentage or grade-point threshold is published for the scholarship; admission thresholds are per course.
eligibility.language_requirement: If English is not the applicant's first language, the English language profile assigned to the chosen course must be met. The profile is shown on each course page, so there is no single score: Profile A requires IELTS Academic 7.5 overall with 7.0 in all skills, Profile B requires 7.0 overall with 7.0 in writing and 6.5 in all other skills (undergraduate), and Profile C requires 6.5 overall with 6.5 in all skills. Tests must be taken within two years of the programme start date and component scores must be met in a single sitting.
eligibility.extracurricular_requirement: Not a formal requirement, but application question 1 asks about special skills and achievements beyond academic studies.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Not a formal requirement; application question 2 assesses ambassadorial potential, including benefit to the applicant's community and networks built.
eligibility.financial_need: Not assessed and not means-tested. However, the total of external funding including the Think Big award must not exceed tuition fees.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Think Big cannot be combined with other University of Bristol funded tuition fee discounts; only the award or discount of higher value is applied (Alumni Discount excepted). If an external award covers full tuition fees the applicant is not eligible for Think Big.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: A University of Bristol study application must have been submitted and an application ID (UCAS ID) received before starting the scholarship form. For the 2026-entry round an offer had to be received before Friday 24 April 2026 or the scholarship application was withdrawn.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Courses in Bristol Dental School and Bristol Medical School are not eligible. Most other undergraduate courses are eligible and are listed on the Think Big Scholarships page. Think Big about Science and Engineering (undergraduate) is limited to Chemistry (BSc) and Physics (BSc) in the Faculty of Science and Engineering; Think Big about Veterinary Science is limited to BVSc and BVSc Accelerated Graduate Entry and funds only three years.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: No fixed percentage or grade-point threshold is published for the scholarship. Entry requirements are set per course and appear in the applicant's formal UCAS offer (for example A-level, IB, BTEC or an accepted international qualification).
academic_requirements.programme_specific_requirements: Entry requirements vary by course and are published in the online course finder as typical offers (with separate contextual offers). The scholarship requires the applicant to meet or exceed the entry requirements stated in their formal UCAS offer by the published date.
selection_factors_may_include: Special skills and achievements beyond academic studies
Ambassadorial potential and contribution to community
Motivation for studying at the University of Bristol and future career plans
academic_requirements.holistic_selection_note: Selection is based on the three written responses in the scholarship application form (maximum 1,000 characters each). No published weighting, minimum grade threshold, interview or portfolio requirement exists, and the University does not publish criteria weightings.

english_requirement.moi_rule: Applicants holding a university-level qualification fully taught and examined in English in any country may meet the requirement with an official Medium of Instruction (MOI) letter from the awarding institution; an ECCTIS English Language Proficiency Statement is also accepted. Nationals of English-speaking countries on the UKVI list are generally exempt, as are applicants who completed the final four years of high school, two years of a full-time bachelor's degree, one year of a master's degree, or two years of a TNE/international partnership degree in an English-speaking country, provided the qualification was awarded within seven years. Qualifications from Ghana, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Singapore, Uganda and Zambia are also accepted. Applicants may also demonstrate ongoing engagement with English through qualifying work experience, and the University reserves the right to refuse an exemption.
english_requirement.test_score_note: The requirement is course-specific, not programme-specific: the University runs eight English language profiles (A-H) and the profile for each course is shown on the course page, so no single minimum score can be stated. Undergraduate figures read from the official profile pages: Profile A - IELTS Academic 7.5 overall with 7.0 in all skills, TOEFL iBT 103 overall (R24, L22, S25, W24) for tests up to 20 January 2026 and 5.5 overall with 5 in all skills from 21 January 2026, PTE Academic 78 overall with no score below 71; Profile B - IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with 7.0 in writing and 6.5 in all other skills, TOEFL iBT 95 overall (R22, L21, S23, W24) or 5 overall from 21 January 2026, PTE Academic 71 overall with no score below 71 in writing and 67 in all other skills; Profile C - IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with 6.5 in all skills, TOEFL iBT 88 overall (R22, L21, S23, W22) or 4.5 overall from 21 January 2026, PTE Academic 67 overall. Duolingo English Test does not appear among the accepted tests on the profile pages examined, so no Duolingo score is recorded.
accepted_tests: IELTS Academic (test centre or online), including One Skill Retake results
TOEFL iBT and TOEFL at Home
Pearson PTE Academic (Test Centre) and Pearson PTE Academic UKVI
LanguageCert Academic and LanguageCert Academic SELT
Pre-sessional English programmes (Bristol, Strathclyde, Heriot-Watt, Warwick, Portsmouth, Kaplan EAP, AEMG Direct Entry Programme)
International Baccalaureate English A and English B
GCSE, IGCSE, AS Level and A Level English
European and international school-leaving qualifications as listed per profile

language_of_instruction.language_note: All eligible undergraduate courses are taught in English. Modern language degrees involve study of another language, but teaching and assessment at Bristol are in English and the course's English language profile still applies.

application_method.application_route: Direct student application through the University of Bristol international scholarships online form, submitted after a UCAS study application; the single form is matched to the study application and considered for every Think Big award for which the applicant is eligible.
application_steps: Apply to study at the University of Bristol through UCAS and receive an application ID (UCAS ID).
Open the international scholarships online application form linked from the Think Big Scholarships page and enter personal details matching the study application.

Answer the three written questions: achievements and special skills beyond academic studies; ambassadorial potential and contribution to community; reasons for studying at Bristol and future career plans. Maximum 1,000 characters including spaces each.
Agree to the data statement, the terms and conditions and the academic integrity statement.
Submit before the published deadline (10:00 am UK time for the 2026-entry round). The application cannot be edited after submission.
Receive a confirmation email (check junk or spam) and await the outcome; for the 2026-entry round outcomes were shared in late May 2026 and award letters in July 2026.

official_application_documents.document_format: Online form (free-text written responses and acceptance of declarations); no uploads are specified on the application guidance page.
official_application_documents.transcript_requirement: Transcripts and qualification certificates are submitted through the UCAS application rather than the scholarship form.
official_application_documents.certified_translation_requirement: English language qualifications must be presented in English; if a qualification is not in English, a professional or certified translation including the translator's or translation company's contact details must be provided.

selection_process.decision_maker: University of Bristol, which matches each scholarship application to the applicant's study application and assesses it against the eligibility criteria of every Think Big award
selection_process.selection_type: Competitive written application assessed centrally through one form; automatic consideration for all eligible awards, but not automatic on admission
possible_stages: Submit the UCAS application and receive an application ID
Submit the Think Big scholarship application before the published deadline
Application matched to the study application and checked against the eligibility criteria of every Think Big award
Assessment of the three written responses and of eligibility conditions (fee status, offer, entry requirements)
Outcomes communicated (late May 2026 for the 2026-entry round) and offer-holder acceptance deadline
Award letters issued (July 2026 for the 2026-entry round) and tuition fee discount applied at enrolment
selection_process.weighting_note: No weighting between academic record and written responses is published, and no marks or scoring system is disclosed.
selection_process.results_timing: Late May 2026 for the 2026-entry round, with a separate offer-holder deadline to accept in late May 2026 and award letters in July 2026.
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: Applicants are considered for every award they are eligible for from a single form. A subject-specific award may be offered alongside or instead of the standard award, and where more than one University-funded tuition fee discount applies only the higher-value award is given.

selection_criteria.academic_excellence: Entry requirements must be met or exceeded, but no separate scholarship grade threshold or ranking is published.
selection_criteria.leadership: Assessed through the ambassadorial potential question, which asks what the applicant might do to benefit their community and how they have built relationships and networks.
selection_criteria.community_service: Referenced in the ambassadorial potential question; not a formal requirement.
selection_criteria.extracurricular_achievement: Referenced in question 1, which asks about special skills and achievements beyond academic studies and the difference the applicant has made.
selection_criteria.financial_need: Not a selection criterion; the award is not means-tested.
selection_criteria.additional_factors: Motivation for studying at Bristol and future career plans. The University states that the use of AI or translation tools is considered cheating, with narrow exceptions for occasional short phrases and basic grammar and spelling checks.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: The undergraduate degree of the course studied (for example BSc, BA, LLB, BEng, MSci, MArts, MLibArts or BVSc). The scholarship confers no separate qualification.
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: 3 to 4 years full-time; longer for integrated master's degrees (MSci, MArts, MLibArts, MEng) and for BVSc Veterinary Science
degree_outcome.degree_note: The standard discount is applied for each year of study up to a maximum of four years. Think Big about Veterinary Science funds only three years of full-time study.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Not applicable. The award applies only to study at the University of Bristol and is not applied during placement, study-abroad or suspension years.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: The award is applied as a discount to tuition fees, adjusted at the time of enrolment; the reduced invoice appears on the recipient's financial statement and no cash alternative is available.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No fee is charged for the scholarship application. The UCAS application fee is separate and is not covered by the award.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Applicants must agree to the University's data statement, the Think Big terms and conditions and an academic integrity statement. Awards are allocated under the published terms and conditions, which the University publishes both as a web page and as a downloadable Office document.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Recipients are invited to join the Think Big Development Programme (welcome reception and online and in-person workshop series) and may apply for paid Think Big Ambassador roles. Recipients are expected to act as ambassadors of the University and to uphold its values and reputation; promotional involvement is limited to a maximum of 10 hours per semester.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: No bond, service obligation or repayment condition is published.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: Not applicable. Where a recipient does not make satisfactory progress (average mark above 50% each year), annual renewal of the fee discount may not apply.

application_readiness_checklist: UCAS application submitted and UCAS application ID in hand
Confirmation of the University of Bristol as intended Firm choice
English language profile identified for the chosen course and a qualifying test result obtained within two years
Three written answers drafted offline, each under 1,000 characters
Terms and conditions and academic integrity statement reviewed
Deadline diarised at 10:00 am UK time for the published closing date
programme_comparison_fields: Years funded (up to four years; three for Think Big about Veterinary Science)
Combination rules with other University-funded fee discounts
practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: The task is three short written answers rather than one long essay. Question 1 rewards specific, verifiable achievement outside the classroom and evidence of impact. Question 2 rewards concrete community contribution and networks built, not generic leadership language. Question 3 rewards a specific account of why Bristol (course, city, community) and a credible career plan. Draft each answer offline, keep within 1,000 characters, and transfer to the form, because the application cannot be edited after submission.
profile_fit_labels: Applicant meeting the course's English language profile
Applicant targeting a subject-specific Think Big award (Business, Economics, Policy Studies, Science and Engineering, Veterinary Science)
Applicant able to fund living costs independently
common_mistakes: Starting the scholarship application before applying to study at Bristol, so no application ID is available
Assuming an offer is required before applying (it is not at the point of scholarship application, but an offer must be held by the published offer deadline)
Using different personal details on the scholarship form and the UCAS application, which breaks the matching process
Using AI tools or machine translation in the written answers, which the University treats as cheating
Leaving Bristol as an Insurance choice rather than the Firm choice
Deferring entry and expecting the scholarship to transfer, which is not permitted
Submitting without proofreading, since the application cannot be changed after submission

risk_flags.risk: The last published deadline (10 April 2026 at 10:00 am UK time) has already passed and no 2027-entry date had been published at the time of verification.
risk_flags.impact: Applicants who plan around the 2026 dates could miss the 2027-entry round entirely.
risk_flags.mitigation: Monitor the official international scholarships page from late October 2026 and apply as soon as the 2027-entry form opens; do not assume the 2026 dates carry over.

risk_flags.risk: Renewal depends on maintaining an average mark above 50% each year.
risk_flags.impact: The fee discount can lapse in later years of the degree.
risk_flags.mitigation: Confirm the annual progression expectations for the chosen course and plan study so the average mark threshold is comfortably met.

risk_flags.risk: The award cannot be combined with other University of Bristol tuition fee discounts.
risk_flags.impact: An applicant holding or offered another University-funded fee discount receives only the higher-value award, reducing the effective benefit.
risk_flags.mitigation: Declare any other University scholarship or fee discount and compare values before accepting.

risk_flags.risk: The award covers tuition only, with no living allowance, travel, installation, visa or insurance support.
risk_flags.impact: Students must independently fund living costs (the University reports average undergraduate living costs of £1,401 per month in 2025/26) plus visa and Immigration Health Surcharge costs.
risk_flags.mitigation: Build a full costed budget covering fees net of the discount, living costs, travel, visa and health surcharge before accepting.

risk_flags.risk: A Bristol offer, firm choice confirmation and entry requirements are conditions of the award, not just of admission.
risk_flags.impact: The scholarship application is withdrawn if no offer is received by the published offer deadline, and the award fails if entry requirements are not met by 31 August.
risk_flags.mitigation: Track UCAS deadlines, confirm Bristol as the Firm choice, and meet or exceed the formal offer conditions by the stated date.

risk_flags.risk: Awards are valid only for September entry of the named year and cannot be deferred.
risk_flags.impact: An applicant who defers their place loses the scholarship.
risk_flags.mitigation: Decide before accepting whether a gap year or deferred entry is intended and plan the scholarship application cycle accordingly.

risk_flags.risk: Award values and the list of subject-specific awards change each year.
risk_flags.impact: Values recorded for 2026 entry may not apply to the 2027-entry round.
risk_flags.mitigation: Re-check the undergraduate awards list and values on the official page when the 2027-entry round is announced.

risk_flags.risk: Eligibility depends on overseas fee status, which is assessed case by case under UK Government regulations.
risk_flags.impact: An applicant later assessed as a Home fee payer becomes ineligible for the award.
risk_flags.mitigation: Check the fee status guidance before applying and verify the fee status stated on any offer as soon as it is issued.

application_status_workflow: Apply to study at the University of Bristol through UCAS
Submit the Think Big scholarship application form before the published deadline
Application matched to the study application and considered for all eligible Think Big awards
Hold an offer from Bristol before the published offer deadline
Receive scholarship outcome (late May for the 2026-entry round) and accept by the offer-holder deadline
Meet or exceed entry requirements and confirm Bristol as Firm choice in UCAS
Enrol at Bristol and have the tuition fee discount applied
Renew the discount each year while making satisfactory progress
best_fit: International applicants with overseas fee status applying to a full-time, in-person undergraduate degree at Bristol, including final-year secondary school applicants, who can write three short and specific answers about achievements beyond the classroom, community contribution and career plans, who can meet their course's English language profile, and who can fund their own living costs and travel.
not_best_fit: Applicants who need a full ride covering living costs, flights, insurance or visa costs
Applicants to Bristol Dental School or Bristol Medical School courses
Applicants who already hold a University of Bristol tuition fee discount or full external tuition funding
Applicants who need to defer entry to a later year
Applicants unwilling to confirm the University of Bristol as their Firm choice in UCAS

database_notes: Naming: the assigned target referred to a 'Think Scholar' scheme. No award by that name exists on bristol.ac.uk. The University's flagship international undergraduate and postgraduate scholarship scheme is officially named 'Think Big', and this record documents that scheme's undergraduate awards under the assigned filename 16-uk-bristol-think-scholar.json.

No substitution was required: the assigned target (University of Bristol international undergraduate scholarships) is not on the do-not-duplicate list in research/bachelor/RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md, so this is the original target rather than a substitute.

Scope: this record covers the undergraduate awards of the Think Big scheme only. The scheme also includes postgraduate awards (including the Think Big Career Accelerator, Think Big about Research, subject-specific postgraduate awards and bursaries such as the Michael Wong Pakshong bursary and the R. Senathi Rajah Memorial Scholarship), which are out of scope for a bachelor's record.

Cycle: the record documents the most recent completed cycle (September 2026 entry), which closed on 10 April 2026. No 2027-entry dates had been published on bristol.ac.uk at the time of verification, so no 2027 deadline is asserted. The 2026-entry timeline (opened 21 October 2025) is the only published precedent for when the 2027-entry round is likely to open.

Deadline handling: deadline_date holds the last published exact deadline (2026-04-10, 10:00 am UK time) and status is CLOSED as required for dates earlier than the verification date, with the next-cycle expectation recorded in status_note.

Dates: last_verified_date, _verification_timestamp, logo_verified_at and image_verified_at use 2026-10-03, the verification date mandated by research/bachelor/SCHEMA_CONTRACT.md, and the ISO timestamps use 09:30 UTC as the time of reading.
Number of awards: not published. Only the aggregate investment (up to £5 million for 2026 entry, up to £6 million stated for 2025 entry) is given, so no award count is recorded.

English language requirements belong to the University's admissions framework (eight course-specific profiles A-H), not to the scholarship. The scholarship does not set its own language scores, so the universal IELTS/TOEFL/PTE fields are null and the observed Profile A, B and C undergraduate scores are recorded in english_requirement.test_score_note instead of being universalised.

Application form hosting: the official pages link the scholarship form to https://internationalscholarships.fillout.com/thinkbig2026, an external form platform. The form is linked from and referenced by the official bristol.ac.uk pages, but the submission page itself is not on the bristol.ac.uk domain.

The terms and conditions are also published as a downloadable Office document at https://www.bristol.ac.uk/media-library/sites/students/documents/think-big-ts&cs-2026.docx (linked from the terms and conditions page as 'Read and save these terms and conditions as a document').

Living-cost context: the average monthly living cost figure (£1,401 for undergraduate students in 2025/26) comes from the University's undergraduate fees and funding page and is recorded only as context; it is not part of the award.
Logo: the official University of Bristol logo is verified on the provider's own domain (bristol.ac.uk). No third-party logo source was used. No photograph asset was verified, so image_url is null.

Not recorded as a benefit: the Think Big Development Programme is a non-cash benefit with published participant survey statistics (100%, 98%, 98%, 96% satisfaction figures from a joint survey with ICOS Consulting). It is described in coverage but carries no monetary value.
_cycle: 2026 entry (closed); 2027 entry not yet published at time of verification
